candidates.description: Do you love hot n sloppy drama? Are you sick and tired of plays in which all the characters have humanity and clear motivations? Then come bear witness to a stunning new work: A highly melodramatic one-act play where you provide the juicy secrets. Tell us about your neighbor’s affair, your sorority sister’s MLM, your grandfather’s secret second family, and watch it all come to life onstage. Drinks will be thrown. Fingers will be pointed. Cigarettes will be brandished. Beans will be spilled. Relationships will not be repaired. It's Tennessee-Williams-meets-Real-Housewives, and it's delicious.

candidates.title: Days of Awe
candidates.venue: Asian Arts Initiative Third Floor
candidates.description:
A year after her mother’s death, a poet in recovery moves home to Philadelphia to get a divorce and start a new life. Set during the ten days from Rosh Hashanah to Yom Kippur, this solo show blends poetry, storytelling, and chutzpah into a lyrical reckoning with grief, the inheritances we carry, and the possibility of reinvention after rupture.
Told with equal parts reverence and irreverence, Days of Awe draws on family history and Jewish ritual to ask how we can carry loss without surrendering desire.

over the 50 sexual assaults in Ovid’s Metamorphoses.

transformations. As literary as it is visceral, as slyly funny as it

candidates.description: Fuck it, I love You is an extension of my work with vignettes, duration and repetition. The work leans in to the ways in which transformation insists upon itself, this takes the pressure off of the idea of a narrative arc and allows the work to function through its own continuity and narrative spaciousness. The work takes on the feeling of a landscape or a softly breathing image.
